records.name: TeenTrek
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that runs workshops, adventure camps and one-on-one mentoring to help teens build life skills.
records.what_you_do: Teens attend workshops on skills such as career exploration, effective communication and financial literacy. Each event has a Details page where you can register.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the Events page, most on Saturdays. Some dates show no year and some are still to be determined.

first_step.how: Call 484-245-4778 or open the Events page and use Details to register for the next workshop. You can also sign up for the mailing list through the site's subscribe form.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public with a registration link on each one. The site does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: Legal name TeenTrek (IRS). Status is unknown: the Events page has a 2024 Event Calendar heading and lists events by weekday and month with no years, so the newest dated evidence cannot be placed within 12 to 24 months. The calendar widget shows October 2026, which is not counted as evidence. The Volunteer link leads to a partner form, not to volunteer roles. The site describes a Facebook community section focused on teenage boys; not read. Events listed in Wilmington and Warminster are outside Philadelphia; the record lists Philadelphia only. IRS street address not published, since the site gives only Philadelphia, PA.

records.name: Museum of Black Joy
records.summary: A museum project that shows art about Black joy through exhibitions, public artworks and a mobile museum.
records.what_you_do: Visit an exhibition or the mobile museum when one is open, or attend a workshop when one is scheduled. The site lists no volunteer roles and no membership.

first_step.how: Check the exhibitions list on the website, then use the Contact page to ask about upcoming events. The page we read shows no email, phone or address.
first_step.basis: The site lists exhibitions without dates and gives no volunteer or membership path, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Legal name Museum of Black Joy Foundation. Dormant is a judgment from year-only dates: the newest dated item is a 2020 artwork credit, and no month is shown, so last_sign_of_life is left out. Exhibitions are listed without dates. The Seeding Joy Workshops link points to a Philadelphia Museum of Art event page, with no date on our copy. The Contact page shows no email, phone or address. Instagram and Facebook links recorded, not read. IRS street address (7301 Brentwood Rd) not published or used.

records.name: Bogucki Foundation
records.summary: A charity that says it runs its own programs in education, health and social welfare, gives grants, and welcomes volunteers and partners.
records.what_you_do: Send a message through the Contact Us form to ask about volunteering or partnering. The site names a Community Education Program and a program called Cops and Bobbers but does not explain how to take part in either.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on boguckifoundation.com to ask which programs take volunteers and how to sign up.
first_step.basis: The site invites volunteers and partners, but it does not describe programs, dates or how to start.

records.notes: Legal name Bogucki Foundation Inc. The page does not say whether this is a private or a public foundation, and does not say where its programs run. If it proves to be a private foundation, our rules make it out of scope, so check before promoting. The IRS record lists a related LLC as contact; not published. The only date on the site is a copyright footer, which is not counted, so probably_active rests on a working site with no dates. IRS address not published or used.

records.name: KIPP Philadelphia Schools
records.summary: A network of public charter schools in Philadelphia. Families join by applying to enroll, not through a community group.
records.notes: Charter school operator with a regional office at 5070 Parkside Ave, which is an office, not a community meeting place. IRS name is KIPP North Philadelphia Charter School; the site uses KIPP Philadelphia Schools. The site says applications for the 2027 to 28 school year are open, with no month shown. KIPP Forward counseling is a service of the school network, not a separate group. Not published.

records.name: Philly Peace in Progress
records.summary: A West Philadelphia nonprofit that offers mentoring, life skills and grocery help to youth, families and older adults, with a focus on young people affected by violence.
records.what_you_do: Find a program through the Get Help page; services run at partner sites such as recreation centers and libraries. Volunteers can use the Volunteer page, though the steps are not described there.

schedule.text: The site lists hours of 4:00 to 7:30 pm on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. The page does not say which services these hours cover.

locations.label: West Philadelphia, at partner sites such as recreation centers and libraries

first_step.how: Call (445) 208-0177 or use the Contact page on the website to ask which program fits you, or start on the Get Help page.
first_step.basis: The site has a Get Help page for finding programs and a phone number to call. Volunteer steps are not explained.

records.notes: IRS name Philly Peace In Progress; the site uses Philly Peace in Progress. The homepage cites early 2026 gun violence figures, the newest dated item we found. It is a statistic, not a dated post, so status is probably_active rather than active. No dated events on the site. Email is shown only behind the Contact page, so not recorded. A personal LinkedIn profile linked from the site is not recorded. A December 2022 Philadelphia Tribune article (not used for status) describes an after-school dance and theater program and gives a 2020 founding. Idealist and Catchafire listings were not used as facts. Events and Volunteer pages not read; a later pass can check them.

records.name: Karima Cares
records.summary: A nonprofit listed with the IRS. We could not find a working website or any public page for it, so what it does and how to join are still unknown.
records.notes: The IRS filing lists karimacares.org as its website. That host did not resolve, with or without www, so the website is treated as missing. This record was not searched: both WebSearch calls went to Team Basketball & Education and Philly Peace in Progress before the cap. No categories, interests, audience or sources were written, so the pipeline should hold it back until checked. Re-run with one search for Karima Cares Philadelphia. Contact name from the IRS filing not published.

notes: Searches: both of the 2 allowed were used, on Team Basketball & Education and Philly Peace in Progress; the cap was then reached, so Karima Cares and Kids In Need were not searched and are placeholders. Fetches: 12. Verdicts: publish 7, not_a_group 1. Four publish records have verified facts from the group's own site or a dated public page (TeenTrek, Museum of Black Joy, Bogucki Foundation, Philly Peace in Progress). Three publish records are placeholders with status unknown and no audience, categories or sources (Karima Cares, Kids In Need Recovered Addicts, Team Basketball & Education); they are expected to be held back by the pipeline until someone checks them, and the orchestrator should decide. KIPP is a charter school operator, not a group. Two IRS website fields were names rather than web addresses (Kids In Need, Philly Peace In Progress); the Philly Peace domain came from its Idealist listing and was then verified on the group's own site. Two IRS domains are dead (Karima Cares, Team Basketball). No IRS street addresses are published: the group pages did not give them, and several look like homes or apartments.
